channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: BoE’s Greene: Warns of second-round inflation effects if we act late
item.description: The comments from Bank of England (BoE) Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) member Megan Greene released during the Asian trade on Tuesday signals that she is worried about second-round inflation effects coming into play if we [central bank] fail to act soon.

item.title: IMF forecasts global real GDP growth of 3.1% in 2026
item.description: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) raised its 2026 global growth forecast to 3.1% from 3.0% in July, with strong AI investment offsetting the energy shock from the Middle East war. However, 2027 growth remained unchanged at 3.4%.

item.title: Japanese Yen strengthens despite softer PPI data
item.description: The USD/JPY pair loses ground to near 158.25 during the Asian trading hours on Tuesday. The Japanese Yen (JPY) strengthens against the US Dollar (USD) despite softer Japanese Producer Price Index (PPI) inflation data.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD falls to near $60.00 amid higher oil prices, US Dollar
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) extends its losses for the second consecutive day, trading around $60.00 per troy ounce during Asian hours on Tuesday. Silver is struggling as rising oil prices fuel inflation concerns, bolstering expectations of further Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hikes.

item.title: United States Dollar Index eases from 18-month peak; slips below 102.50
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which tracks the Greenback against a basket of currencies, drifts lower during the Asians session on Tuesday, eroding a part of the previous day's strong gains to a fresh high since April 2025.

item.title: Euro gathers strength above 1.1150 despite France’s fiscal concerns
item.description: The EUR/USD pair gains ground to near 1.1165 during the early Asian trading hours on Tuesday. Nonetheless, the potential upside for the major pair might be limited amid growing fiscal and political instability in France. All eyes will be on the key US inflation reports later this week.

item.title: British Pound gains on BRC Like-For-Like Retail Sales data despite geopolitical tensions
item.description: GBP/USD inches higher after posting modest losses in the previous day, trading around 1.3220 during Asian hours on Tuesday. The pair appreciated as the British Pound (GBP) gained ground following the release of British Retail Consortium (BRC) Like-For-Like Retail Sales data.

item.title: Canadian Dollar edges higher but remains close to April 2025 lows vs bullish USD
item.description: The USD/CAD pair edges lower during the Asian session on Tuesday, though it remains close to the highest level since April 2025, touched last week. Spot prices currently trade around the 1.4270 region as a bullish US Dollar (USD) helps limit the downside.

item.title: PBOC sets USD/CNY reference rate at 6.7298 vs. 6.7313 previous
item.description: The People’s Bank of China (PBOC) sets the USD/CNY central rate for the trading session ahead on Tuesday at 6.7298 compared to the previous day's fix of 6.7313 and 6.6981 Reuters estimate.

item.title: WTI holds gains above $91.50 as Russia attacks Ukrainian power plant
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI), the US crude oil benchmark, is trading around $91.50 during the early Asian trading hours on Tuesday. WTI price edges higher amid growing doubts of an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine and a deadly attack on Saudi Arabia’s airport in Riyadh.

item.title: RBA Minutes: Case for rates to act promptly to keep inflation expectations anchored
item.description: Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) published the Minutes of its September monetary policy meeting on Tuesday, with the key takeaways noted below.

item.title: Aussie Dollar struggles at 0.70, retreats as Oil shock boosts the USD
item.description: The Australian Dollar ended Monday’s session with losses of close to 0.40% amid thin liquidity due to the Columbus Day holiday, with most US cash markets closed, as market participants were guided by the latest geopolitical developments. The AUD/USD trades near 0.6950 after peaking below 0.7000.

item.title: US Envoy Kushner says diesel deal is an effort to soften Russia
item.description: US special envoy Jared Kushner said that a deal to allow Russian diesel exports is part of a bid to draw Russia back to negotiations after the failure of previous efforts to launch sustained talks to end the war, Reuters reported on Monday.

item.title: Saudi Arabia says drones and missiles still targeting kingdom as Houthis step up attacks
item.description: Saudi Arabia said that it faces more drones and missile strikes, while several countries issued travel warnings against visiting the kingdom following deadly strikes on Riyadh’s airport by Iran-backed Houthi militants, CNBC reported on Monday.

item.title: Gold tumbles below $4,200 on higher oil prices, firmer US Dollar
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) falls to around $4,170 during the early Asian session on Tuesday. The precious metal retreats from a ‌one-week high on a stronger US Dollar (USD) and higher crude oil prices.

item.title: The Japanese Yen slips on a Tokyo holiday
item.description: Brent climbed above $107 a barrel on Monday with Japan shut for the Health and Sports Day holiday and the US government bond market shut for Columbus Day. USD/JPY closed near 158.60, its highest close since September 24, and its low for the day came within minutes of Brent's.

item.title: The British Pound drifts back to its floor as Crude Oil lifts the Dollar
item.description: Every session since September 24 has bottomed within about 25 pips of 1.3200, and Monday was the 13th. GBP/USD closed near 1.3210 after a climb to just above 1.3250, made before London opened, was given back as Brent rose above $107 a barrel.

item.title: Euro collapses below 1.12 as Fed hawkish rhetoric lifts the US Dollar
item.description: The Euro extends its losses against the US Dollar on Monday, even falling below the psychological 1.1200 level as sellers step in following hawkish comments from a Fed policymaker and growing geopolitical concerns on two fronts: the US-Iran war and Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.

item.title: Fed’s Hammack sees thriving economy, backs further rate hikes
item.description: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said that further tightening is needed but reiterated earlier remarks that she is open “to adjusting the pace of rate increases.”

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average edges higher with no memory chips to sell
item.description: Micron fell about 4% on Monday and the NASDAQ 100 fell with it, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA), which holds no memory-chip maker, finished higher. The S&P 500, which holds Micron and all 30 Dow members, finished slightly lower.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Building upside momentum toward 6.6800 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note USD/CNH unexpectedly fell to 6.6919 on Friday, with downside momentum starting to build. Intraday, they see potential for a brief dip below 6.6900, provided the pair stays under 6.6985. Over 1–3 weeks, a clear break and close beneath 6.6900 could open the way toward 6.6800, while resistance is now at 6.7050.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar hits 17-month high, RBA minutes and Fed speaking up next
item.description: Buyers are stepping in and keeping the US Dollar (USD) bid due to safe-haven demand, as the resumption of hostilities in the Middle East and strikes between Russia and Ukraine have pushed energy prices higher.

item.title: Gold tumbles as Oil shock fuels US Dollar rally and Fed hike bets
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) price drifts lower by about 1.49% on Monday as the Greenback gains ground amid escalating hostilities in the Middle East, pushing energy prices higher and increasing the likelihood of higher interest rates globally.

item.title: South Korean Won: Uptrend seen resuming against US Dollar – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale strategists note that the recent USD/KRW bounce stalled around 1390 and the pair is now testing the lower end of its consolidation, suggesting the broader downtrend may resume.

item.title: WTI hits two-week high Middle East tensions overshadow Russian diesel supplies
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Oil reverses course on Monday and climbs to a two-week high as doubts over a Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire and supply concerns in the Middle East keep a geopolitical premium in energy markets.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Gradual appreciation with trade pressures – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman notes the Chinese Renminbi has outperformed the Euro against the Dollar, with USD/CNY hitting a year-to-date low near 6.6900. PBoC’s lower daily fixes have supported trade‑weighted CNY gains.

item.title: Fed’s Hammack sees higher neutral rate, urges more policy restraint
item.description: Cleveland Federal Reserve (Fed) President Beth Hammack said on Monday that the neutral rate for the Fed funds “is likely higher,” that she is hearing signs of a problem with inflation expectations and that the question for the Fed is “how fast to make policy more restrictive.”

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Range bias holds near 1.2835 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note USD/SGD was little changed around 1.2800 on Friday and expect consolidation to persist. Intraday, they see the pair confined between 1.2790 and 1.2820, with 1.2775 as strong support. Over the next few weeks, upward momentum is rebuilding but seen too weak for a sustained break above 1.2835.

item.title: Fed’s Hammack calls for higher rates as inflation pressures broaden
item.description: Cleveland Federal Reserve (Fed) President Beth Hammack said Monday that interest rates need to be higher, that inflation remains “too high”, and that more economic tightness is needed.

item.title: Swedish Krona: Riksbank outlook supports SEK against Euro – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley discusses EUR/SEK, noting Sweden’s resilient economy, stronger-than-expected GDP and a hawkish shift at the Riksbank.
